According to arXiv 2608.25839, conflict zone capability transfers primarily affect the success rate of catastrophic terrorism attempts by providing battlefield-tested skills that make attempted attacks more likely to succeed. However, it is unlikely to increase the attempt rate, as capability transfer improves execution rather than underlying motivation.

AI-assisted attack planning, on the other hand, is likely or probable to increase both the attempt rate and success rate. AI lowers the knowledge barrier for attack planning, enabling more actors to attempt attacks (increasing the attempt rate) and improving the quality of plans for those already motivated (increasing the success rate). The severity of attacks remains limited due to execution barriers that still need to be overcome.
